nodes.text: Harken Vos peers up, parchment tilted toward his working eye. 'Rider. State your business, please. Succinctly. I am half-blind, not half-deaf, and if you mutter, you forfeit.'

options.text: I have a bounty claim to file.
You've seen a lot of claims, clerk. Anything strange lately?

nodes.text: 'A bounty. Good. There is, in point of fact, one the roster has been *conspicuously* unable to fill. A wayhouse burning near Reed-End. Two dead, one missing. The suspect description is — and I quote the original complainant — "mean-looking." I have declined to transcribe this. I require a Rider willing to ride out, observe, and return with particulars a reasonable clerk can enter into the ledger.'

options.text: Sounds like Gravenguard work, not mine.
Why hasn't the Gravenguard handled this?

nodes.text: Harken's pen stops. 'Because, Rider, the original complainant is the Gravenguard. And the suspect description, I suspect, is a deflection. I would like a Rider's eyes on it, not a Guardsman's. That is all I shall say on that in this room.'

'Excellent. I will log this as — ' his pen hovers — ' "Rider engaged; particulars pending." Return within a sevennight. If you do not, I shall be forced to record that you failed to return, and I would prefer not to write those words about you.'
Harken nods, already writing. 'Safe roads, Rider. And for the record: "irregardless" is not a word. Do not use it in your report.'
'I see. Very well. I shall log this exchange as — ' his pen twitches — ' "Rider declined; particulars unpursued." Good day.'
Harken looks up, then down again. 'The Reed-End matter. You have not yet returned particulars. I am required to ask: are you still engaged with the claim, or should I re-list?'
'Noted. I shall leave the ledger line open. Please do not make me close it in your absence.'
Harken sets aside the claim roll and pulls a *second* ledger — unmarked, kept low in the drawer. 'Proceed. I shall determine which of these two books receives your account.'

options.text: The suspect was a Gravenguard footman. Varn's man.
It was exactly who the complaint said it was.

nodes.text: The unmarked ledger opens. Harken writes rapidly, left-handed, both hands shaking, only one admitting it. 'Thank you, Rider. This will be… filed appropriately. You have my gratitude and — ' he slides two silver coins across the desk — ' a modest honorarium I am not, technically, authorized to disburse. Take them anyway.'
'Mm. Transcribed. The claim is closed.' His pen scratches once, decisively, in the *public* ledger. The unmarked ledger stays shut. 'Good day, Rider.'
Harken blots the page. 'Safe roads.' He does not look up.

He pauses. Sets the pen down flat — the rare tell. 'Strange, Rider, is a category, not an observation. But — since you ask, and since I trust you to ask *properly* — yes. Three claims this month were filed by complainants who, upon verification, did not exist. Names correct. Seals correct. Persons: absent. I am told this is not my concern.'

options.text: Thank you. I'll keep ears open.

nodes.text: ' *Varn*. Each time. I have not written that down. I am, however, saying it aloud to you, which is arguably worse. Please do not give me cause to regret it.'
Harken does not look up. 'Rider. State your business. Do not use contractions; I find them, in the current climate, unreliable. I am writing.'
'I shall transcribe what you say. I shall not vouch for it. Proceed.'
